items.title: fix(api): refuse redirects that turn a write into a GET
items.body:
## Description

When a proxy in front of GitLab answers an `http` request with a redirect to `https`, `glab release create` fails with `cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type gitlab.Release`, which is the error in #8095. net/http follows a 301, 302 or 303 answer to a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE by sending a GET to the new location without the body, so the create reaches the list releases endpoint instead. An update is worse: the GET reaches the release itself, decodes into the expected type, and glab prints `Release updated` although nothing was changed.

This MR gives the HTTP client built in `internal/api/client.go` a `CheckRedirect` policy, in the new `internal/api/redirect.go`:

- A redirect that keeps the method is followed as before: every redirect of a GET or HEAD, and a 307 or 308 of a write, which resends the body.
- A redirect that would change the method is refused, with an error that names the status and the URL that redirected.
- When that redirect moves the same host from `http` to `https`, the error also says to set `api_protocol` to `https`. In a CI job like the one in #8095 that is the `GLAB_API_PROTOCOL: https` variable, or, as the triage note says, an `external_url` with `https`, so that `CI_SERVER_PROTOCOL` is `https` too. With CI auto-login on (`GLAB_ENABLE_CI_AUTOLOGIN=true`), glab reads the protocol from `CI_SERVER_PROTOCOL` alone, so `GLAB_API_PROTOCOL` does not help there.
- The limit of 10 redirects is kept, because setting `CheckRedirect` replaces the default policy that enforced it.

Everything that shares this client gets the policy, for example: client-go, the OAuth2 login flows and token refresh, and `glab api`. GitLab's own redirects are not affected: it answers a write to a moved project with 405 rather than a redirect ([`lib/api/helpers.rb`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/f46efbab1af9e65bfa5f7bbd9bb7fd3ecf323307/lib/api/helpers.rb#L184-187) in gitlab-org/gitlab), and when it forwards a package registry POST it uses 307 ([`lib/api/helpers/packages/dependency_proxy_helpers.rb`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/f46efbab1af9e65bfa5f7bbd9bb7fd3ecf323307/lib/api/helpers/packages/dependency_proxy_helpers.rb#L23-24)), which keeps the method.

<details>
<summary>Before and after, with the built binary</summary>

I built glab from `main` (8ae0c0ef5) and from this branch, and ran `glab release create v1.0.0 -R <host>/group/project --notes "new notes" --name v1.0.0` with `GLAB_API_PROTOCOL=http` against a stand-in GitLab on `https`, behind a stand-in proxy on `http` that answers every request with a 301 to `https`.

The release does not exist yet, so glab creates it.

`main`, exit 1. After the proxy's 301, glab sent `GET .../releases` in place of the `POST`:

```plaintext
ERROR
Json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type gitlab.Release.
```

This branch, exit 1, and the `POST` never reaches GitLab (the error as glab prints it, unwrapped):

```plaintext
Post "https://127.0.0.1:34627/api/v4/projects/group%2Fproject/releases": refusing to follow the 301 redirect from http://127.0.0.1:46093/api/v4/projects/group%2Fproject/releases, which would resend this POST request as a GET without its body; the server redirects http to https, so set api_protocol to https.
```

The release exists, so glab updates it.

`main`, exit 0, and GitLab received `GET .../releases/v1%2E0%2E0` in place of the `PUT`:

```plaintext
✓ Release updated	url=https://example.invalid/r
✓ Release succeeded after 0.00 seconds.
```

This branch, exit 1:

```plaintext
Put "https://127.0.0.1:41851/api/v4/projects/group%2Fproject/releases/v1%2E0%2E0": refusing to follow the 301 redirect from http://127.0.0.1:35035/api/v4/projects/group%2Fproject/releases/v1%2E0%2E0, which would resend this PUT request as a GET without its body; the server redirects http to https, so set api_protocol to https.
```

</details>

## Related Issues

Resolves #8095

The same failure was reported for `glab mr create` in #7728, closed for inactivity, and in gitlab-org/api/client-go#2094. `glab mr create` goes through the same client, so it gets the refusal too; client-go itself does not change here.

## How has this been tested?

`internal/api/redirect_test.go` drives the client `NewClient` builds against a real `httptest` server:

- A create answered with 301 and an update answered with 302 are refused, and nothing reaches the redirect target. Both fail on `main`: the create with the error from #8095, the update with no error at all.
- A GET answered with 301 is followed, and a create answered with 308 is followed with its body intact.
- A redirect loop stops after 10 redirects.
- The `api_protocol` hint appears for `http` to `https` on the same host, and not for another host or for a redirect that keeps the scheme. This test fails on `main` too.

Checks I ran with Go 1.27.1:

- `go test` on `internal/api/...`, `internal/oauth2/...`, `internal/commands/api/...`, `internal/commands/auth/...` and `internal/commands/release/...`, and `go test -race ./internal/api/...`
- `make test`: 5515 tests, all passing apart from the 17 the suite skips
- `golangci-lint run` with 2.14.0: no findings in the changed files
- `go run ./scripts/comment-overlap -threshold 1.0 -max-findings 0 ./cmd/... ./internal/...`: 0 findings
- `make build`, `make check-embed` and `make check-args`
- the login line GitLab's release job runs (`glab auth login --job-token ... --api-protocol $CI_SERVER_PROTOCOL`) with `http`, against a stand-in GitLab that only speaks `https`: `glab api version` then used `http`, with `GLAB_API_PROTOCOL=https` it used `https`, and with `GLAB_API_PROTOCOL=https` under CI auto-login it still used `http`
- commitlint with `scripts/commit-lint`'s rules on the commit message and on this title

issue.title: Add a way to close milestones
issue.body:
### Problem to solve

Right now you can do the basic CRUD operations on milestones, but you can not close them.

### Proposal

Add a new flag: `glab milestone edit XXX --close` that would close the given milestone.

### Further details

Our milestones work on a time based, so whenever the period finishes, we create new milestones, move open work items to the these new milestones and finally we close the old milestones.

So far we can do all of it but the last part, closing milestones.

### Links / references

items.title: `host` config key / GITLAB_HOST overrides repo remotes instead of acting as a fallback
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)
  - Also reproduced from source at main (`glab DEV`)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? _both_
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) _v19.3.3_
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

The top-level `host:` key in `config.yml` (or the `GITLAB_HOST` / `GITLAB_URI` / `GL_HOST` environment variables) is treated as an **override when inside a Git repository** instead of as a default for when no host can be resolved. When the key differs from the repo's remote host, glab filters the remotes down to the configured host and fails all repo-bound commands. The key is documented as "Default GitLab instance, outside Git repositories", so it should only apply when the remote (or a URL argument) doesn't determine the host.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)

### Steps to reproduce

With no network required (the failure happens before any API call):

```sh
git init /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro
git remote add origin https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli.git
mkdir -p /tmp/cfg && cat > /tmp/cfg/config.yml <<'EOF'
git_protocol: https
host: gitlab.tuwien.ac.at
hosts:
  gitlab.tuwien.ac.at:
    token: fake
    api_protocol: https
    git_protocol: https
EOF
chmod 600 /tmp/cfg/config.yml
GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg glab issue list
```

Setting `host:` to anything other than `gitlab.com` (or setting `GITLAB_HOST`) triggers the filter in any repo whose remote points to a different instance.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

1. The command fails with `None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable` even when **no** environment variable is set and the value came from the `host:` key — the error message is misleading.
2. With `-R OWNER/REPO` (no host in the argument), the request silently goes to the configured instance instead of the repo's remote host, targeting the wrong instance and token.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

- Inside a Git repository, the remote (or a URL argument) determines the host; the `host:` key / `GITLAB_HOST` are only fallbacks when the host cannot be resolved (e.g. outside a repo).
- The error message should say which source set the override (config key vs. env var).

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

```
$ GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg GLAB_DEBUG=true glab issue list
2026/10/08 19:04:51 [Could not determine base repo in telemetry hook:  none of the git remotes
configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable. Try adding
a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

Configured remotes: gitlab.com]

   ERROR

  None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST
  environment variable. Try adding a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

  GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

  Configured remotes: gitlab.com.
```

(Note: in the debug log line, the trailing `]` closes the `GLAB_DEBUG` log entry, which wraps the message in brackets; it is not part of the error text.)

### Possible fixes

- `internal/cmdutils/factory.go`: `defaultHostname` is set from `cfg.Get("", "host")` before `BaseRepo()` resolves; `Remotes()` then sets `hostOverride` whenever the default differs from `gitlab.com` (\~line 192).
- `internal/cmdutils/remote_resolver.go`: the `hostOverride` block (\~lines 103-127) drops all non-matching remotes, then errors out.
- `RepoOverride` (`factory.go`) resolves `-R OWNER/REPO` against `defaultHostname` instead of the repo's remote host.
- Note: `remote_resolver_test.go` (\~line 428) locks in the current override behavior, so this needs a decision on intended semantics (env var as hard override vs. fallback), not just a test change.
- Related: #8084 covers the URL-host case of the same host-resolution model.

items.title: Accept relative dates (-7d, 2w) in list date filters, and add date filters to issue list
items.body:
### Problem to solve

Date filters in glab only take absolute timestamps, and each command parses them differently:

- `glab mr list --created-after/--created-before/--deployed-after/--deployed-before` take RFC3339 only (added in #8124).
- `glab ci list --updated-after/--updated-before` take only the exact layout `2019-03-15T08:00:00Z`.
- `glab issue list` has no date filters at all, even though the REST API supports `created_after`, `created_before`, `updated_after` and `updated_before`.

So everyday questions like "issues updated in the last week" or "MRs created in the last 30 days" need a date computed in the shell, which is awkward in scripts and aliases (`date -d` vs. BSD `date -v`).

### Proposal

1. Add one shared date flag type that accepts:
   - absolute dates: `2026-10-01` and RFC3339 (`2026-10-01T08:00:00Z`)
   - relative dates in the [GLQL syntax](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/glql/#values): an optional sign, a number and a unit (`d`, `w`, `m`, `y`). `-7d` is 7 days ago, `2w` is 2 weeks from now.
2. Resolve relative values on the client to the start of that day in the local time zone, then send an absolute timestamp. This works with every GitLab version, with no API change.
3. Use it for the existing `mr list` and `ci list` date flags (backwards compatible, since current inputs keep working).
4. Add `--created-after`, `--created-before`, `--updated-after` and `--updated-before` to `glab issue list`.

Example:

    glab issue list --updated-after -7d
    glab mr list --created-after -1m --created-before -1w

### Further details

- Values that start with `-` look like flags. pflag accepts both `--flag=-7d` and `--flag -7d`, but both forms deserve a test and a help-text example.
- Using GLQL's syntax keeps glab consistent with what GitLab already documents for GLQL queries.
- Related discussion about relative dates in GitLab's GraphQL filters: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/260072#note_3973533253

### Links / references

- #8124 (absolute before/after filters for `mr list`)
- GLQL relative dates: https://docs.gitlab.com/user/glql/#values
- REST issues API filters: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/issues/#list-issues

### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.121.0 (4d447cc6c)
- [x] Operating system and version: Aurora 44.20260929.1, based on Fedora 44 Kinoite (Linux 7.1.10-200.fc44.x86_64)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 19.4.1-ee
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output
  - `GLAB_DEBUG=true` prints nothing beyond the error below.

### Summary

On a large MR, GitLab stores only part of the diff, and `changes_count` is reported with a `+` suffix (`"N+"`). `glab mr note create --file <path> --line <n>` looks the file up only in that stored list, so for any of the remaining files it fails with `file "<path>" not found in MR diff`, even though the file is part of the MR. A diff comment on the same path and line succeeds when posted directly with `POST /projects/:id/merge_requests/:iid/discussions` and a `position` built from the latest version's SHAs.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.1.10-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.121.0 (4d447cc6c)

Other: none

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an MR whose diff exceeds the instance's diff limits, so that `GET /projects/:id/merge_requests/:iid` reports `changes_count` with a `+` suffix (`"N+"`).
2. Pick a changed file that is not among the stored ones: it is missing from `GET .../merge_requests/:iid/versions/:version_id` (`diffs`) and from the paginated `GET .../merge_requests/:iid/diffs`, but present in `GET .../merge_requests/:iid/raw_diffs`.
3. Run `glab mr note create <iid> --file <that/path> --line <added line> -m "test"`.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

```
ERROR
File "<that/path>" not found in MR diff.
```

No comment is created.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

The diff comment is created on the given file and line, like it is with a direct API call. If glab cannot place it, the error should say the MR diff is truncated (`changes_count` "N+") rather than that the file isn't in the MR.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

```
$ GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr note create <iid> --file <that/path> --line 10 -m "test"

   ERROR

  File "<that/path>" not found in MR diff.
```

The same comment posted directly through the API is accepted and anchored correctly:

```shell
glab api -X POST "projects/:id/merge_requests/<iid>/discussions" \
  -F body=@comment.md \
  -F 'position={"position_type":"text","base_sha":"<base>","start_sha":"<start>","head_sha":"<head>","new_path":"<that/path>","old_path":"<that/path>","new_line":10}'
```

The created discussion has `position.new_path` = `<that/path>` and `position.new_line` = 10.

### Possible fixes

[`GetLatestDiffVersion`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/4d447cc6c19858928884626d802c8f7b7c5f799e/internal/commands/mr/mrutils/position.go#L16) reads the file list from `GetSingleMergeRequestDiffVersion`, and [`FindFileDiff`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/4d447cc6c19858928884626d802c8f7b7c5f799e/internal/commands/mr/mrutils/position.go#L34-41) fails when the path isn't in `version.Diffs`. For a truncated diff, the structured endpoints never list the file, so pagination alone won't help.

# GLab

![GLab](docs/source/img/glab-logo.png)

GLab is an open source GitLab CLI tool. It brings GitLab to your terminal, next to where you are already working with `git` and your code, without switching between windows and browser tabs. While it's powerful for issues and merge requests, `glab` does even more:

- View, manage, and retry CI/CD pipelines directly from your CLI.
- Create changelogs.
- Create and manage releases.
- Ask GitLab Duo Chat (Classic) questions about Git.
- Manage GitLab agents for Kubernetes.

`glab` is available for repositories hosted on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab Self-Managed. It supports multiple authenticated GitLab instances, and automatically detects the authenticated hostname from the remotes available in your working Git directory.

![command example](docs/source/img/getting-started.gif)

## Table of contents

- [Requirements](#requirements)
- [Usage](#usage)
  - [Commands](#commands)
  - [GitLab Duo for the CLI](#gitlab-duo-for-the-cli)
- [Demo](#demo)
- [Documentation](#documentation)
- [Installation](#installation)
  - [Homebrew](#homebrew)
  - [Other installation methods](#other-installation-methods)
  - [Building from source](#building-from-source)
    - [Prerequisites for building from source](#prerequisites-for-building-from-source)
- [Authentication](#authentication)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Environment variables](#environment-variables)
  - [Debugging](#debugging)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
- [Issues](#issues)
- [Security](#security)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
  - [Versioning](#versioning)
  - [Classify version changes](#classify-version-changes)
  - [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [Inspiration](#inspiration)

## Requirements

`glab` officially supports GitLab versions 16.0 and later. Certain commands might require
more recent versions. While many commands might work properly in GitLab versions
15.x and earlier, no support is provided for these versions.

## Usage

To get started with `glab`:

1. Follow the [installation instructions](#installation) appropriate for your operating system.
1. [Authenticate](#authentication) into your instance of GitLab.
1. Optional. Configure `glab` further to meet your needs:
   - 1Password users can configure it to [authenticate to `glab`](https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/shell-plugins/gitlab/).
   - Set any needed global, per-project, or per-host [configuration](#configuration).
   - Set any needed [environment variables](#environment-variables).

You're ready!

### Commands

Run `glab --help` to view a list of core commands in your terminal.

<!-- commands-list-start: generated by 'make gen-docs'; do not edit by hand -->
- [`glab alias`](docs/source/alias): Create, list, and delete aliases.
- [`glab api`](docs/source/api): Make an authenticated request to the GitLab API.
- [`glab artifact-registry`](docs/source/artifact-registry): Authenticate with GitLab Artifact Registry. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab attestation`](docs/source/attestation): Manage software attestations. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab auth`](docs/source/auth): Manage authentication for glab.
- [`glab changelog`](docs/source/changelog): Generate changelogs from your project's commit history.
- [`glab check-update`](docs/source/check-update): Check for the latest glab version.
- [`glab ci`](docs/source/ci): Work with GitLab CI/CD pipelines and jobs.
- [`glab cluster`](docs/source/cluster): Manage GitLab Agents for Kubernetes and their clusters.
- [`glab completion`](docs/source/completion): Generate shell completion scripts.
- [`glab config`](docs/source/config): Manage glab settings.
- [`glab container-registry`](docs/source/container-registry): Work with GitLab container registries.
- [`glab dependency-firewall`](docs/source/dependency-firewall): Configure and monitor GitLab Dependency Firewall for local package managers. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab deploy-key`](docs/source/deploy-key): Manage deploy keys.
- [`glab duo`](docs/source/duo): Work with GitLab Duo.
- [`glab govern`](docs/source/govern): Manage AI agent governance. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab gpg-key`](docs/source/gpg-key): Manage GPG keys registered with your GitLab account.
- [`glab incident`](docs/source/incident): Work with GitLab incidents.
- [`glab issue`](docs/source/issue): Work with GitLab issues.
- [`glab iteration`](docs/source/iteration): Retrieve iteration information.
- [`glab job`](docs/source/job): Work with GitLab CI/CD jobs.
- [`glab label`](docs/source/label): Manage project and group labels.
- [`glab mcp`](docs/source/mcp): Work with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab milestone`](docs/source/milestone): Manage group or project milestones.
- [`glab mr`](docs/source/mr): Create, view, and manage merge requests.
- [`glab opentofu`](docs/source/opentofu): Work with the OpenTofu or Terraform integration.
- [`glab orbit`](docs/source/orbit): Run the GitLab Orbit CLI. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab packages`](docs/source/packages): Manage packages in the GitLab package registry.
- [`glab release`](docs/source/release): Manage GitLab releases.
- [`glab repo`](docs/source/repo): Work with GitLab repositories and projects.
- [`glab runner`](docs/source/runner): Manage GitLab CI/CD runners.
- [`glab runner-controller`](docs/source/runner-controller): Manage runner controllers. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab schedule`](docs/source/schedule): Work with GitLab CI/CD schedules.
- [`glab search`](docs/source/search): Search for code and resources in a GitLab project. (BETA)
- [`glab securefile`](docs/source/securefile): Manage secure files for a project.
- [`glab security`](docs/source/security): Manage GitLab security scan profiles for a project. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab skills`](docs/source/skills): Manage glab agent skills. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab snippet`](docs/source/snippet): Create snippets.
- [`glab ssh-key`](docs/source/ssh-key): Manage SSH keys registered with your GitLab account.
- [`glab stack`](docs/source/stack): Create, manage, and work with stacked diffs. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab todo`](docs/source/todo): Manage your to-do list.
- [`glab token`](docs/source/token): Manage personal, project, or group tokens.
- [`glab user`](docs/source/user): Interact with a GitLab user account.
- [`glab variable`](docs/source/variable): Manage variables for a GitLab project or group.
- [`glab version`](docs/source/version): Show version information for glab.
- [`glab whatsnew`](docs/source/whatsnew): Show release notes for new versions of glab.
- [`glab work-items`](docs/source/work-items): Manage work items. (EXPERIMENTAL)
<!-- commands-list-end -->

Commands follow this pattern:

```shell
glab <command> <subcommand> [flags]
```

Many core commands also have sub-commands. Some examples:

- List merge requests assigned to you: `glab mr list --assignee=@me`
- List review requests for you: `glab mr list --reviewer=@me`
- Approve a merge request: `glab mr approve 235`
- Create an issue, and add milestone, title, and label: `glab issue create -m release-2.0.0 -t "My title here" --label important`

### GitLab Duo for the CLI

The GitLab CLI also includes support for using the GitLab Duo Agent Platform directly in your terminal.

Use `glab duo cli` to ask GitLab Duo questions about your codebase and to autonomously perform actions on your behalf.

For more information, see [GitLab Duo CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/gitlab_duo_cli/).

## Demo

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/368622.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/368622)

## Documentation

Read the [documentation](docs/source/_index.md) for usage instructions or check out `glab help`.

## Installation

Download a binary suitable for your OS at the [releases page](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases).
Other installation methods depend on your operating system.

### Homebrew

Homebrew is the officially supported package manager for macOS, Linux, and Windows (through [Windows Subsystem for Linux](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install))

- Homebrew
  - Install with: `brew install glab`
  - Update with: `brew upgrade glab`

### Other installation methods

Other options to install the GitLab CLI that may not be officially supported or are maintained by the community are [also available](docs/installation_options.md).

### Building from source

If a supported binary for your OS is not found at the [releases page](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases), you can build from source:

#### Prerequisites for building from source

- `make`
- Go version as defined by [`main/go.mod`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/go.mod?ref_type=heads#L3)

To build from source:

1. Run `go version` to verify that you have the minimum required Go version.
   If Go is not installed, see [Download and install](https://go.dev/doc/install).
1. Clone the repository: `git clone https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli.git`
1. Build the binary: `make build`
1. Install `glab` in `$GOPATH/bin`: `make install`
1. Optional. If `$GOPATH/bin` or `$GOBIN` is not in your `$PATH`,
   run `export PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH`.
1. Confirm the installation: `glab version`

## Authentication

To authenticate `glab` with OAuth, a personal access token, or a CI job token, see
[Authenticate with GitLab](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/).

## Configuration

For configuration levels, the configuration search order, and platform-specific file
locations, see [Configure the CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/configuration/).

For connecting to a GitLab Self-Managed or GitLab Dedicated instance, and for mTLS and
self-signed certificates, see
[Connect to your GitLab instance](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/connection/).

For authenticating proxies, including custom HTTP headers and Google Identity-Aware
Proxy, see [Connect through a proxy](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/proxies/).

## Environment variables

`glab` reads its configuration from environment variables as well as the configuration
file. Every configuration key has a matching variable, and the variable wins over the
stored value. Setting them centrally is a good way to give everyone in an organization
the same setup.

For the full reference, see
[Environment variables](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/configuration/#environment-variables).
For how `glab` picks which token to use, see
[Token precedence](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/#token-precedence).

### Debugging

When the `GLAB_DEBUG` environment variable is set to `true`, `glab` outputs more logging information, including:

- Underlying Git commands.
- Expanded aliases.
- DNS error details.

## Troubleshooting

For help with common authentication issues, see
[Troubleshooting](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/#troubleshooting) in the GitLab CLI documentation.

## Issues

If you have an issue: report it on the [issue tracker](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues)

## Security

To report a security vulnerability in `glab`, follow the process in
the [security policy](SECURITY.md). Please do not open a public issue.

To learn how the project handles dependency updates and container-scanner CVE
reports, see [dependency management](CONTRIBUTING.md#dependency-management)
and [reporting a vulnerability](CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-a-vulnerability)
in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Contributing

Feel like contributing? That's awesome! We have a [contributing guide](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of conduct](https://about.gitlab.com/community/contribute/code-of-conduct/) to help guide you.

When updating command help text or documentation, follow the
[GitLab CLI documentation style guide](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/documentation/cli_styleguide/).

### Versioning

This project follows the [SemVer](https://github.com/semver/semver) specification.

### Classify version changes

- If deleting a command, changing how it behaves, or adding a new **required** flag, the release must use a new `MAJOR` revision.
- If adding a new command or **optional** flag, the release must use a new `MINOR` revision.
- If fixing a bug, the release must use a new `PATCH` revision.

### Compatibility

We do our best to introduce breaking changes only when releasing a new `MAJOR` version.
Unfortunately, there are situations where this is not possible, and we may introduce
a breaking change in a `MINOR` or `PATCH` version. Some of situations where we may do so:

- If a security issue is discovered, and the solution requires a breaking change,
  we may introduce such a change to resolve the issue and protect our users.
- If a feature was not working as intended, and the bug fix requires a breaking change,
  the bug fix may be introduced to ensure the functionality works as intended.
- When feature behavior is overwhelmingly confusing due to a vague specification
  on how it should work. In such cases, we may refine the specification
  to remove the ambiguity, and introduce a breaking change that aligns with the
  refined specification. For an example of this, see
  [merge request 1382](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/1382#note_1686888887).
- Experimental features are not guaranteed to be stable, and can be modified or
  removed without a breaking change.

Breaking changes are a last resort, and we try our best to only introduce them when absolutely necessary.

## Inspiration

The GitLab CLI was adopted from [Clement Sam](https://gitlab.com/profclems) in 2022 to serve as the official CLI of GitLab. Over the years the project has been inspired by both the [GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli) and [Zaq? Wiedmann's](https://gitlab.com/zaquestion) [lab](https://github.com/zaquestion/lab).

Lab has served as the foundation for many of the GitLab CI/CD commands including `ci view` and `ci trace`.

items.title: `host` config key / GITLAB_HOST overrides repo remotes instead of acting as a fallback
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)
  - Also reproduced from source at main (`glab DEV`)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? _both_
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) _v19.3.3_
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

The top-level `host:` key in `config.yml` (or the `GITLAB_HOST` / `GITLAB_URI` / `GL_HOST` environment variables) is treated as an **override when inside a Git repository** instead of as a default for when no host can be resolved. When the key differs from the repo's remote host, glab filters the remotes down to the configured host and fails all repo-bound commands. The key is documented as "Default GitLab instance, outside Git repositories", so it should only apply when the remote (or a URL argument) doesn't determine the host.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.120.0 (78790114c)

### Steps to reproduce

With no network required (the failure happens before any API call):

```sh
git init /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro
git remote add origin https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli.git
mkdir -p /tmp/cfg && cat > /tmp/cfg/config.yml <<'EOF'
git_protocol: https
host: gitlab.tuwien.ac.at
hosts:
  gitlab.tuwien.ac.at:
    token: fake
    api_protocol: https
    git_protocol: https
EOF
chmod 600 /tmp/cfg/config.yml
GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg glab issue list
```

Setting `host:` to anything other than `gitlab.com` (or setting `GITLAB_HOST`) triggers the filter in any repo whose remote points to a different instance.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

1. The command fails with `None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable` even when **no** environment variable is set and the value came from the `host:` key — the error message is misleading.
2. With `-R OWNER/REPO` (no host in the argument), the request silently goes to the configured instance instead of the repo's remote host, targeting the wrong instance and token.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

- Inside a Git repository, the remote (or a URL argument) determines the host; the `host:` key / `GITLAB_HOST` are only fallbacks when the host cannot be resolved (e.g. outside a repo).
- The error message should say which source set the override (config key vs. env var).

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

```
$ GLAB_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/cfg GLAB_DEBUG=true glab issue list
2026/10/08 19:04:51 [Could not determine base repo in telemetry hook:  none of the git remotes
configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST environment variable. Try adding
a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

Configured remotes: gitlab.com]

   ERROR

  None of the git remotes configured for this repository correspond to the GITLAB_HOST
  environment variable. Try adding a matching remote or unsetting the variable.

  GITLAB_HOST is currently set to gitlab.tuwien.ac.at

  Configured remotes: gitlab.com.
```

(Note: in the debug log line, the trailing `]` closes the `GLAB_DEBUG` log entry, which wraps the message in brackets; it is not part of the error text.)

### Possible fixes

- `internal/cmdutils/factory.go`: `defaultHostname` is set from `cfg.Get("", "host")` before `BaseRepo()` resolves; `Remotes()` then sets `hostOverride` whenever the default differs from `gitlab.com` (\~line 192).
- `internal/cmdutils/remote_resolver.go`: the `hostOverride` block (\~lines 103-127) drops all non-matching remotes, then errors out.
- `RepoOverride` (`factory.go`) resolves `-R OWNER/REPO` against `defaultHostname` instead of the repo's remote host.
- Note: `remote_resolver_test.go` (\~line 428) locks in the current override behavior, so this needs a decision on intended semantics (env var as hard override vs. fallback), not just a test change.
- Related: #8084 covers the URL-host case of the same host-resolution model.

items.title: Impossible to configure_docker, since container_registry_domains is not stored when --use-keyring is supplied and also not checked

### Summary

Using `glab auth login` with `--use-keyring` does not store the survey answer to supplied container registry domains.

Additionally `glab auth status` does not check for validity of container registry credentials.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Login with `glab auth login --use-keyring` and provide container registry domains
2. Try to do `glab auth configure-docker`
3. See the error

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The error is thrown:

```
ERROR: no hosts were configured - ensure you've logged in via oauth2 and configured at least one container registry domain for a host
```

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

`configure_docker` succeeds and container registry domains are retained when using the keyring, as without using `--use-keyring`.

Else the error could also be more understandable, such as "no container registries found in configuration retrieved from keyring/configuration file at path …".
